correctness.rationale: Marked ordered cycles give E C_j=Z(n-j,2)/(jZ(n,3)), E(C_j C_k)=Z(n-j-k,1)/(jkZ(n,3)) for j≠k, where Z(m,h)=[m h]/m!. With k=n-j-r, r=floor(c√n), identities Z(m,1)=1/m, Z(m,2)=H_{m-1}/m and Z(m,3)=(H²_{m-1}-H^{(2)}_{m-1})/(2m) yield exact sign determinant D=1/2(H_{n-1}²-H_{n-1}^{(2)})−[nr/((n-j)(j+r))] H_{n-j-1}H_{j+r-1}. Expanding harmonic numbers for fixed j,c gives D=−(log c+γ/2)log n−γ log c−γ²/2−π²/12+o(1); at c=e^-γ/2 the constant is −π²/12<0. Substituting Z(n,3)~(log n)²/(2n) derives the two stated distinct covariance normalizations. Independently enumerated three-cycle permutations through n=7 and checked 40 bounded comparisons including critical-scale digamma signs. The floor error is O(1/√n) and does not change equality boundary.
residual_risks: Distinct j and k required; fixed j,c pointwise asymptotic only.
The finite enumeration is not evidence of the n→∞ sign law, which comes from explicit harmonic expansion.

value.rationale: The constrained sample space of three-cycle permutations naturally couples a fixed short cycle to a nearly spanning one. Determining whether their counts attract or repel, exactly where the sign switches on a √n leftover scale, and why the critical case loses a logarithmic order is a mathematically informative asymptotic classification, not merely repackaging Stirling numbers.
residual_risks: No uniformity over j,c and no all-finite-n sign pattern is asserted.

final_claim: For permutations conditioned to have exactly three cycles, covariance of C_j and C_{n-j-floor(c√n)} changes sign at c=e^-γ/2, with a strictly negative critical boundary and distinct (log n)^-3 versus (log n)^-4 scales.
limitations: j and c fixed as n→∞; two marked cycle lengths distinct for sufficiently large n.
Classical marked factorial moments are acknowledged antecedents; older equivalent conditional asymptotics remain possible.
